newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo gold ends slightly lower, platinum firms.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo gold ends slightly lower, platinum firms.

text.p: TOCOM yen-based gold futures ended barely lower on Friday, in line with a dip in bullion prices, although platinum futures managed a firmer finish as they corrected from Thursday's decline, traders said.

They tended to take a mildly bearish short-term view of the markets, however, noting sluggish demand in Japan, while a modest rally in the first half of this month from multi-year lows had apparently run out of steam.
TOCOM most-active August 1997 gold settled one yen lower at 1,356 yen per gram, while the other months were one lower to two firmer.

Yen-based futures received little direction from the foreign exchange markets, which held steady throughout the TOCOM session, although after the close the yen slumped to its lowest against the dollar in nearly three years.
Spot gold ended at $380.10/40 an ounce, off from New York's $380.35/85 close and Tokyo's Thursday close at $380.60/90.
After the Tokyo close, bullion prices dipped below the $380 support level and one bullion dealer said they were likely to retest $378, where buying should emerge and offer support.
Traders said there was no influence on the market from Thursday's firing of Russian security chief Alexander Lebed.
TOCOM benchmark August platinum ended four higher at 1,373 yen per gram, while the other months were one to four better.
Traders said short covering helped to lift the market after Thursday's declines, which narrowed the TOCOM platinum-gold spread to 12 yen per gram.

TOCOM August palladium settled one yen lower at 417 yen per gram, attempting to build a base after spot prices slid this week to three-year lows amid slack Japanese demand and steady sales out of Russia, traders said.
August silver ended off 3.0 yen at 179.3 yen per 10 grams.
